params.body:
Both delete buttons on the damage tab did nothing on staging: the one on a damage block and the one on a damage photo. The pencil next to them worked.

## What was wrong

Both controls carried

```blade
onclick="owConfirmDeleteDamage('…', '…', 'damage', @json($part));"
```

`@json` writes a JSON string with real double quotes, and the attribute is delimited by double quotes. The HTML parser ends a double-quoted attribute at the first double quote in its value, so the browser got

```
owConfirmDeleteDamage('http://…/deletedamage/Mjg0Mjk1', '#image_block_284295', 'damage', 
```

which is a syntax error, and an inline handler with a syntax error never runs. No console error at load, nothing at the click. The pencil on the line above has no `@json` in its `onclick`, which is exactly why it still worked.

Confirmed before changing anything: the damage tab was rendered for a vehicle with damage and a damage photo and the markup read back with `DOMDocument`. The attribute came back truncated, one closing paren and one argument short, on all three controls.

This is the same failure as X-96 (a double quote inside a double-quoted Alpine attribute), one attribute family further.

## The fix, and why this one

Three options were on the table: `@js()` instead of `@json`, a data attribute read by the handler, or binding the click in JavaScript. The part name is **text, not code**, so the root fix is to stop putting it inside a piece of JavaScript at all. `@js()` would have been one token and would have worked, but it keeps the shape that bit us: a string literal inside an attribute value, one careless edit away from the same failure.

So the controls now carry their data and not their call:

```blade
<a data-ow-delete="damage" data-ow-url="…" data-ow-target="#image_block_…" data-ow-part="{{ $dmgPlek }}">
```

and `damage.blade.php` binds the click, delegated on `document`. Delegated because `#damages` and the photo list in the dialog are reloaded over AJAX after every save: a listener per button is gone after the first one. The binding is guarded so a page that renders the partial twice does not ask twice.

`owConfirmDeleteDamage` itself is unchanged, so the wording still works: "Schade aan motorkap verwijderen?" from the part name, and the empty/`'extra'` case still means collecting place 18 with its own sentence. Verified in the browser for both (screenshots below).

Three places carried this, not two: the damage block and the photo in the list (`damages.blade.php`), plus the photo in the dialog (`_damage_media.blade.php`), which `addDamage` renders on its own.

## Closing the hole

`AlpineExpressionTest` scans Blade views for an Alpine attribute whose value cannot be a complete expression. `onclick` is not an Alpine attribute, so the guard added this afternoon never looked at the place where the same failure sat the next day. It now also scans the whole `on*` family (`onclick`, `onchange`, `onsubmit`, `onerror`, …) with the same three signals — brackets out of balance, an unterminated block comment, an odd number of single quotes — plus a fourth: an emitter whose output is **not** escaped for an attribute (`@json`, `{!! !!}`) standing inside a double-quoted one.

It has to read the value the way the parser does, not grep for quotes. A first, naive version flagged **26** places over the view tree, of which 23 were false positives from `{{ trans("global.duplicate") }}`: a double quote that is Blade syntax and never reaches the browser. The scan therefore masks Blade constructs first (`{{ }}`, `{!! !!}`, `@directive(…)`) and only then applies the signals.

After masking it flags **3** places over the whole view tree, and they are the three broken ones this PR fixes:

```
resources/views/ownstock/_tabs/damages.blade.php:16      onclick -> @json() writes unescaped output
resources/views/ownstock/_tabs/damages.blade.php:39      onclick -> @json() writes unescaped output
resources/views/ownstock/_tabs/_damage_media.blade.php:14 onclick -> @json() writes unescaped output
```

Zero after the fix, so the test is green on this branch and does not ship a failure on main. Checked that it bites: putting the old `damages.blade.php` back makes it fail with both line numbers named. Extending it is adding a name to `RAW_EMITTERS` or a signal to the list in the loop.

`custom.delete()` / `custom.ask()` in `resources/js/custom.js` were checked too. They do not build inline handlers themselves, and their call sites pass everything through `{{ }}`, which escapes. Nothing else in the tree builds an inline handler containing `@json`.

## Tests

- `DamageTabTest::test_every_delete_control_on_the_damage_tab_survives_the_parser` renders the damage tab through the Livewire sheet for a vehicle with damage, a damage photo and a place-18 entry, and reads every control back with `DOMDocument` — the parser that truncates exactly as a browser does. Each control has to hand back its kind, address, target and part name, place 18 has to arrive as `extra`, and no `onclick` may be left. This is the assertion that would have caught it: the old markup makes it fail on the first count (1 control instead of 3). Tagged `@rule S1-6.24`.
- `AlpineExpressionTest::test_no_inline_event_handler_is_ended_early_by_a_quote_in_its_value` is the scan above.

## Verified in the running application

Not a component rendered in isolation: the app was started against its own database, logged in as a dealer, the vehicle sheet opened, the Schade tab clicked.

- The photo bin asks "Foto van schade aan motorkap verwijderen?" — the part name reaches the wording.
- The place-18 bin asks "Overige schade verwijderen?" — the collecting-place wording.
- Confirming removes the row from the list and the diagram stops marking the place.

## Docs

- `X-101` in `docs/bedrijfsregels/90-x-bevindingen.md`, with the lesson: the guard added this afternoon covered Alpine attributes only, and the same failure lives in every inline handler.
- New rule `R S1-6.24` in `docs/bedrijfsregels/11-s1-wagen-invoeren-en-beheren.md`, around the existing damage rules (S1-6.15 to S1-6.18).
- `bin/rules-coverage` was run to check it still parses; its output now goes to the gitignored `92-testdekking-tabel.md`, and `docs/bedrijfsregels.html` is generated and no longer in git (PR 329), so neither is in this commit.

`php artisan test --filter='Damage|AlpineExpression|OwnStockRowMarkup|StylesheetSyntax|VehicleForm|RulesCoverage'`: 36 tests, 799 assertions, green. With `Dialog|UiApiUsage` alongside (the dialog component this uses, touched by another PR this evening): 39 tests, 814 assertions, green.
